passage: On Monday, Lokesh's older sibling Baljeet shouted, "Give it back!" and pushed Lokesh off the cushion. Lokesh sat on the floor, feeling very small, and said nothing. On Wednesday, Baljeet raised a fist over the toy truck again. This time Lokesh ran to Mummy and said, "Baljeet pushed me and my arm hurts." On Friday, Mummy sat both children down and asked Baljeet first, then Lokesh, listening to each one. "No pushing, ever," she said. Baljeet's eyes were wet. Lokesh leaned against Mummy and felt a little bigger.

qa.q: Who did Lokesh run to on Wednesday?
qa.a: Lokesh ran to Mummy.

qa.q: How did Lokesh feel on the floor after being pushed on Monday?
qa.a: Lokesh felt very small and helpless, and was too stunned to speak. Saying nothing shows how overwhelmed Lokesh was.

qa.q: What went right on Wednesday, and what should Mummy do when she hears such news?
qa.a: Lokesh told a parent about being hurt instead of keeping it in. Mummy can stop the pushing and hear both children out, as she did on Friday.

qa.q: What might Baljeet have been feeling when Mummy listened on Friday?
qa.a: Baljeet may have felt ashamed and also relieved to be heard, since Mummy asked Baljeet first. The wet eyes suggest Baljeet did care about the hurt.

grounding: A small child is shouted at and pushed by an older sibling, feels helpless, tells a parent, and the parent stops the hurting and listens to both.

passage: The bus was due in five minutes, and Kamal was racing Rukmini to the door. "I'm first!" he shouted, one sock still half on, and he slapped the handle a heartbeat before her. His chest puffed out. Then Rukmini beat him to the shoe rack, calling, "Papa, look, I'm ready!" Kamal's face crumpled and his lip shook. Papa knelt to tie both pairs of laces. "You both moved fast today. Kamal, tonight is your story time with me. Rukmini, yours is tomorrow." Kamal sniffed, nodded, and picked up his bag.

qa.q: How many minutes were left before the bus was due?
qa.a: The bus was due in five minutes.

qa.q: What was Kamal feeling when Rukmini beat him to the shoe rack?
qa.a: Kamal felt crushed. His crumpled face and shaking lip show how much losing hurt after the pride of winning at the door.

qa.q: What did Papa do that could ease the racing between the two children?
qa.a: Papa praised how fast they both moved and gave each child their own story time. That way Papa's attention does not depend on who is first. 🙂

qa.q: What might Rukmini want when she calls, "Papa, look, I'm ready!"?
qa.a: Rukmini probably wants Papa to notice her, just as Kamal does. She may also enjoy winning the shoe race in the same way he enjoyed the door.

grounding: Two young siblings race to be first and compete for Papa's attention; one feels proud in winning and crushed in losing, and Papa gives each child special time and praises effort.

passage: Deepak and Mahima had both been crying in the courtyard, over a wooden bullock cart that Mahima had grabbed and Deepak had pulled back. Amma was cooking rotis and left them alone. Deepak wiped his nose on his sleeve. He walked to where Mahima sat by the water pot and held out the cart. "Sorry I pulled it," he said. "You can play first." Mahima took it and gave a small smile. Deepak felt his chest go light again, like a kite let out on a string. Soon both were rolling the cart along the mud step.

qa.q: What toy were Deepak and Mahima fighting over?
qa.a: They were fighting over a wooden bullock cart.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel after saying sorry and handing over the cart?
qa.a: Deepak felt light again, like a kite let out on a string. Giving the toy along with the words made the sorry real to him.

qa.q: Why was Deepak's sorry a good repair, and what could a parent do when one child will not say sorry?
qa.a: Deepak's sorry came with a kind act, giving the cart, and it came after he had calmed down. A parent could wait until the child feels ready instead of forcing the word.

qa.q: What might Mahima have felt when Deepak held out the cart?
qa.a: Mahima was probably relieved and a little surprised. Her small smile and taking the cart suggest she accepted the sorry.

grounding: After both siblings cried, one hands over a toy and says sorry, feels light again, showing sorry plus a kind act as a repair.

passage: My name is Tara and I am in the same class as Mridul. At playtime a big boy grabbed Sumit's cap and held it up high. Sumit is Mridul's brother. This morning on the bus they were shouting at each other, so I thought Mridul would go away. But he walked over and stood right next to Sumit. His hands were shaking a little, but maybe he was just cold, I don't know. He said, "Give it back." Then he took Sumit's hand and they went to tell Miss. I saw them talking to her.

qa.q: What did the big boy take from Sumit?
qa.a: The big boy grabbed Sumit's cap.

qa.q: What might Mridul have been feeling as he stood beside Sumit?
qa.a: Mridul may have been scared but wanted to protect his brother. Tara notices his shaking hands but says she cannot be sure, so it is only a clue.

qa.q: What did Mridul do that was wise, and what else could he try?
qa.a: Mridul stood by Sumit and then went to tell Miss instead of fighting. If the boy keeps bothering them, they can keep telling a teacher. 👍

qa.q: How might Sumit see it when Mridul stands next to him?
qa.a: Sumit may feel safe and cared for, even though they were shouting on the bus. It shows that being brothers can matter more than an argument.

grounding: A child stands with a brother on the playground despite a morning fight at home, and they tell a teacher rather than fight, seen by a classmate.

passage: Note from the class teacher. At pick-up today, Avni's drawing was torn and she was crying. Jomon said, "She took my crayon first." Their father answered, "You are older, you should know better." Jomon went quiet, folded his arms, kicked at the gravel and would not look up. On the walk to the gate he muttered, "It's not fair." I asked their father if we could hear from both children together before deciding. He agreed, crouched down, and let Jomon speak first. Jomon's shoulders slowly dropped. I will check in with both children tomorrow.

qa.q: What did their father say to Jomon at pick-up?
qa.a: Their father said, "You are older, you should know better."

qa.q: What does Jomon's behaviour after that suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: Jomon felt the blame was unfair and was sulking. Folding his arms, kicking gravel, and muttering "It's not fair" all point to that.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped, and what could the father try next time?
qa.a: The teacher asked that both children be heard before deciding. Next time the father could ask each child what happened before saying who is at fault.

qa.q: How might Avni see the moment when her father lets Jomon speak first?
qa.a: Avni may see that her brother is also being listened to, and that her father wants to know what really happened. She may feel less alone in her tears too.

grounding: A parent blames the older child with "you are older, you should know better", the child feels it is unfair and sulks, and a wiser adult hears both children.

passage: The school in Kalpur sat under a big neem tree, and children sat on jute mats. Farhan looked at Naveen, who was sitting next to him. His heart was thumping so loudly he thought she might hear it. He held up his bag of shiny pebbles. "Do you want to play?" he asked in a small voice. Naveen looked at the pebbles and nodded. "Yes!" Farhan grinned and stood up straight. They threw the pebbles into the circle drawn in the dust, taking turns, and Farhan forgot about his heart altogether.

qa.q: What did Farhan hold up when he asked Naveen to play?
qa.a: Farhan held up his bag of shiny pebbles.

qa.q: How did Farhan feel as he asked Naveen and after she said yes?
qa.a: He was nervous first, and then brave and happy. His thumping heart shows the nerves, and the grin and straight back show his joy.

qa.q: What did Farhan do well in making a friend, and what could he do if she had said no?
qa.a: He made the first move kindly, even though he was shy. If she had said no, he could try again another day or ask another child.

qa.q: What might Naveen have thought when Farhan spoke in a small voice?
qa.a: Naveen may have seen that he was a bit shy and felt glad to be asked. She said yes at once and looked at the pebbles with interest.

grounding: A young child likes a classmate and shyly asks her to play, feeling brave and happy when she says yes.

passage: Note from the nursery teacher. During free play, Naveen stood at the edge of the sandpit for a long while, holding his spade and watching. He did not speak. When I knelt beside him he whispered, "Nobody sees me." We practised together: "Can I play too?" He said it twice, softly. Next day I stood nearby while he tried it on Farhan, who was building a sand fort. Farhan said, "Yes, bring your spade!" Naveen smiled with his whole face and stepped in. He has some way to go, and that is fine.

qa.q: Where did Naveen stand during free play?
qa.a: Naveen stood at the edge of the sandpit.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling when he whispered, "Nobody sees me"?
qa.a: Naveen wanted to join in but felt unnoticed and unsure how to start. Waiting at the edge and whispering suggests shyness, not a lack of wanting.

qa.q: How did the teacher help Naveen, and what small step could come next?
qa.a: The teacher practised the words "Can I play too?" with him and stayed nearby while he tried it. A next step could be trying the words with a small group. 🙂

qa.q: How might Farhan see Naveen's question?
qa.a: Farhan may simply be happy to have another builder for the sand fort. He said yes at once and invited Naveen to bring the spade.

grounding: A shy child waits at the edge of play, and a wise adult helps practise asking to join, showing shyness as something that grows lighter with safe tries.

passage: At lunch in the school hall, Omar carried his tray past the long bench, not sure where to sit. Ivan waved both arms. "Here! I saved you a seat," he said, patting the bench. Then he leaned close. "You are my best friend." Omar felt warm all over and sat down carefully so as not to squash the coat Ivan was guarding. Ivan whispered that he had a wobbly tooth and did not want anyone else to know. Omar nodded and said, "I won't tell." He shared his apple slices.

qa.q: What did Ivan do to save a seat for Omar?
qa.a: Ivan patted the bench and guarded it with a coat.

qa.q: How did Omar feel when Ivan called him best friend?
qa.a: Omar felt warm all over, special and secure, because Ivan had chosen him and kept a place for him.

qa.q: What did Omar do to choose Ivan back, and how could he keep the tooth secret kindly?
qa.a: Omar shared his apple slices and promised not to tell. He can keep it kindly by not teasing Ivan and by not bringing it up in front of others.

qa.q: What might Ivan have wanted when he told Omar about the wobbly tooth?
qa.a: Ivan probably trusted Omar and wanted to share something private with a friend. Whispering shows he did not want the others to hear.

grounding: A child is told he is a best friend and given a saved seat, feels special and secure, and answers by choosing back and keeping a secret kindly.

passage: In the nursery room, Abhinav stood by the coat pegs with his lip trembling. Irfan's peg was empty. "He's not here," Abhinav said, and tears dropped onto his shirt. He would not touch the puzzle table or the paints, and pushed away every hand. The teacher sat beside him. "Irfan will come back. Shall we build a tower with Meera and Joy? You can be in charge of the red bricks." Abhinav wiped his face, watched the others, and slowly took a red brick. He still glanced at the door, but he stacked three bricks before snack time.

qa.q: Whose coat peg was empty?
qa.a: Irfan's peg was empty.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling when he stood at the coat pegs?
qa.a: Abhinav felt sad and lost without Irfan. His trembling lip, his tears, and turning away from every activity show it.

qa.q: How did the teacher help Abhinav, and why does it matter?
qa.a: The teacher offered a small group and a job with the red bricks. This helps Abhinav see he can have other friends, so his day does not depend on one child.

qa.q: How might Meera and Joy feel about Abhinav joining their tower?
qa.a: They may be curious and happy to have another builder. They may not know why he was crying, so being kind and simple is enough.

grounding: A child cries when his best friend is absent and refuses to play with others, and a wise adult helps him join a small group.

passage: It was raining hard, so playtime was inside the crowded classroom. The teacher was busy fixing a jammed cupboard, and there was only one basket of toys. Pankaj saw Uma sitting on the rug laughing with a new girl, Gita, over a doll. A burning feeling rose in his chest. "She is not allowed to play," he said loudly. Gita's smile disappeared. Uma stared at him. Pankaj looked at the floor, took a breath and said, "I felt sad when you played with her. Can we all play?" Uma scooted over to make room.

qa.q: Why was playtime inside the classroom?
qa.a: It was raining hard, so playtime was inside.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling when he said "She is not allowed to play"?
qa.a: Pankaj felt hurt and jealous, like a burning in his chest, because Uma was laughing with someone new. The words came out as excluding, not as his real feeling.

qa.q: What worked in Pankaj's second try, and what went wrong in the first?
qa.a: In his second try he said he felt sad and invited Uma and Gita, which repaired things. His first try tried to keep his friend by shutting Gita out, which hurt her. 🤔

qa.q: How might Gita see the moment Pankaj first spoke?
qa.a: Gita may have felt unwelcome and confused, since she had only just joined in. Her smile disappearing shows the words stung.

grounding: A child feels a burning jealousy when a best friend plays with a new girl, first excludes her, then names the sad feeling and invites both.
